analysis: The PR only changes docs/provider/cli-reference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds one table row at head line 572 documenting a `--prompt-prep` benchmark mode. The row says the mode is CPU-only, loads only the tokenizer, times prompt preparation, prints JSON, and exits 2 on any token-ID or decoded-field difference. The reviewed base units (lines 405-1348) contain no other changes. This is documentation only, so no code, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or coordinator-protocol behavior changes. I examined the prefix-cache threat T-041, the only definition supplied in full, and the new row does not touch it. The row mentions a 'prompt token cache' with background comparisons off, which is a new cache concept that does not appear in T-041's scope (the SSD KV prefix cache). The new benchmark source is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify what that cache stores, whether it persists to disk, or whether it is tenant-scoped. If a new prompt-token cache is added in the provider, the threat model may need an entry covering at-rest or cross-tenant exposure. The supplied evidence is only a documentation line, so I report this as an unverified contract rather than a finding. Next passes should check PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift and any prompt token cache implementation for plaintext prompt persistence, keying and scoping (A-001, T-041, TB-007).
